records.title: Cryopreservation of Rat Islets of Langerhans: A Comparison of Two Techniques
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible IntechOpen islet cryopreservation review on 2026-03-23. The review explicitly describes the DMSO versus ethylene glycol comparison from the original rat study and supports function plus transplantation, but the source is secondary rather than the original abstract.

excerpts.label: comparison review note
excerpts.text: An accessible review of islet cryopreservation summarizes the original rat comparison study as a head-to-head test of dimethyl sulfoxide versus ethylene glycol cryoprotectants rather than a generic freezing paper.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: The same review states that dimethyl sulfoxide-treated rat islets showed impaired insulin secretory patterns and lower cellular insulin and glucagon than ethylene glycol-treated islets, while ethylene glycol-treated islets more closely resembled non-frozen controls.

excerpts.label: transplant review note
excerpts.text: The review further reports that normal glycemic control after transplantation was achieved in all ethylene glycol-treated and non-frozen islets, whereas dimethyl sulfoxide-treated islets corrected diabetes less consistently and with slower recovery.

records.title: Improvement of Human Islet Cryopreservation by a p38 MAPK Inhibitor
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed directly from the accessible American Journal of Transplantation full text on 2026-03-21. Added only conservative manual-note excerpts that make post-thaw outcomes and p38-inhibitor step context explicit.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Human islets were split across RPMI, ICS, and ICS-p38IH groups. For freezing, islets were exposed to 0.5 M DMSO for 20 min, then to 2.1 M DMSO on ice, loaded into chilled cryotubes, and moved into a computer-controlled cryounit starting at 4 C. In the ICS-p38IH arm, SD-282 was added at 0.3 uM in the cryopreservation and thawing media and at 0.1 uM during post-thaw culture.

excerpts.label: results review note
excerpts.text: Post-thaw recovery at day 2 was highest in the ICS-p38IH group, while viability remained similar across RPMI, ICS, and ICS-p38IH. Beta-cell number, morphology, and glucose-stimulated function were best preserved with ICS-p38IH compared with the other frozen groups.

excerpts.label: transplant results review note
excerpts.text: After transplantation into NODscid mice, glucose-stimulated human C-peptide from ICS-p38IH islets reached about 86 percent of nonfrozen controls by 4 weeks. In diabetic recipients, 4 of 5 mice receiving ICS-p38IH islets became and remained euglycemic through day 90, whereas most RPMI and ICS recipients did not reverse diabetes.

records.title: Isolation and Long Term Preservation of Pancreatic Islets from Mouse, Rat and Guinea Pig
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract explicitly reports histological and glucose-stimulated functional survival, so this paper is promotable for viability and function but not transplantation.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: The paper tested three preservation systems for isolated islets from mouse, rat, and guinea pig, including simple cold storage, controlled freezing with dimethyl sulfoxide and serum, and organ culture.

excerpts.label: viability review note
excerpts.text: The abstract reports histological survival after storage and freezing, including roughly 35 percent survival in one freezing group and about 87 percent survival in a second freezing group with a post-thaw culture period.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: Functional survival was assessed by insulin release in response to glucose. The freezing condition with post-thaw culture retained about 75 percent functional survival, while a slower condition retained about 20 percent.

records.title: Pancreatic islets from non-heart-beating donor pig: Two-layer preservation method in an in vitro porcine model
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible abstract snippet on 2026-03-23. The source supports viability and function in a transplant-adjacent porcine isolation context, but not transplantation.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: The study compares preservation methods for pancreatic islets from non-heart-beating donor pig in an in vitro porcine model, including a classic ice-storage approach and a two-layer preservation method before islet isolation.

excerpts.label: viability review note
excerpts.text: The accessible abstract states that islet cell viability could be efficiently preserved during the processing window needed for organ handling.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: The accessible abstract also states that total islet yield and function measured by insulin release favored the preservation strategy being evaluated, indicating transplant-adjacent functional relevance without proving transplantation outcomes.

records.title: Polyvinyl Pyrrolidone: A Novel Cryoprotectant in Islet Cell Cryopreservation
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-22. Added conservative paraphrased notes to make the comparator cryomixes, recovery, and glucose-stimulated function explicit.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Isolated rat islets were frozen with a programmable controller after overnight culture using one of four cryomixes: 2 M DMSO, 3 M glycerol, 5 percent polyethylene glycol, or 10 percent polyvinyl pyrrolidone. Samples were stored at minus 80 C for 1 week and assessed after thawing plus overnight recovery culture.

excerpts.label: recovery review note
excerpts.text: Post-thaw intact islet recovery was higher with polyvinyl pyrrolidone than with DMSO, about 82 percent versus about 63 percent. Recovery with polyethylene glycol was similar to polyvinyl pyrrolidone, while DMSO and glycerol performed worse.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion after freezing with polyvinyl pyrrolidone or polyethylene glycol remained comparable to freshly isolated islets, unlike the DMSO and glycerol groups. The paper concludes that polyvinyl pyrrolidone is a potent cryoprotectant for islet freezing.

records.title: Prolonged Cryopreservation of Purified Human Pancreatic Islets
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract explicitly reports post-thaw recovery, glucose-stimulated perifusion, and preserved morphology/ultrastructure, so this paper is promotable for viability, function, and morphology.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Purified human pancreatic islets were cryopreserved with stepwise 2 M DMSO, supercooled to minus 7.5 C, nucleated, cooled at 0.25 C per minute to minus 40 C, and then stored in liquid nitrogen for a median of 46.5 days.

excerpts.label: viability review note
excerpts.text: The abstract reports about 94 percent recovery by count and about 90 percent recovery by insulin extraction immediately after thawing, with substantial recovery still present after an additional 48 hours in culture.

excerpts.label: function and morphology review note
excerpts.text: Glucose-stimulated perifusion retained normal baseline and first-phase insulin secretion after cryopreservation, although second-phase insulin secretion decreased. Insulin staining and electron microscopy showed preserved morphology and ultrastructure.

records.title: Successful Cryopreservation of Fetal Porcine Proislets
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract supports viability, function, and transplantation-grade in vivo performance.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Fetal porcine proislets were equilibrated with 2 M dimethyl sulfoxide, supercooled, nucleated, cooled at 0.25 C per minute to minus 40 C, and then plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage.

excerpts.label: transplant review note
excerpts.text: After transplantation, all mice receiving cultured fetal porcine proislets and seven of eight mice receiving cryopreserved fetal porcine proislets achieved normoglycemia, with no significant difference between groups.

excerpts.label: function and viability review note
excerpts.text: Grafts from normoglycemic recipients secreted insulin during in vitro perifusion, and histology showed comparable in vivo differentiation and development between cryopreserved and cultured groups. The abstract concludes that the protocol maintained functional viability after thawing.

records.title: Successful Long-Term Cryopreservation of Highly Purified Canine Islets
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible European Surgical Research abstract on 2026-03-23. The title plus abstract support a conservative viability reading, but not function or transplantation.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Highly purified canine islets were equilibrated by hypothermic treatment and stepwise exposure to 2 M dimethyl sulfoxide, seeded near minus 7.8 C, slowly cooled at 0.25 C per minute from minus 10 C to minus 40 C, and then plunged into liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.

excerpts.label: viability review note
excerpts.text: The title explicitly frames the protocol as successful long-term cryopreservation of highly purified canine islets. Conservatively, that supports post-thaw survival or viability after storage, but it does not by itself establish functional or transplantation outcomes.

records.title: Vitrification of Mouse Islets of Langerhans: Comparison with a More Conventional Freezing Method
records.rationale: title/abstract suggests a positive result but does not state a concrete benchmark-safe outcome class
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-22. Added conservative paraphrased notes to make the comparative design and the in vitro plus in vivo outcomes explicit.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: The study compared mouse islets preserved by vitrification with a cryoprotectant mixture against islets frozen in 1.5 M Me2SO, alongside unfrozen cultured controls. Both cryopreserved groups were rewarmed and cultured for 4 days before outcome testing.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: After warming, both cryopreserved groups still showed strong glucose-responsive insulin secretion. High-glucose secretion was only slightly lower than controls and survival during post-warm culture was comparable between vitrification and conventional freezing.

excerpts.label: transplant review note
excerpts.text: Islets from both cryopreserved groups lowered serum glucose in streptozotocin-diabetic mice, supporting preserved in vivo graft function. The authors conclude that vitrification preserved mouse-islet function in vitro and in vivo while avoiding complex freezing equipment.

records.title: Bulk Cryopreservation of Isolated Islets of Langerhans
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-22. Added conservative paraphrased notes to make the bulk-banking workflow, recovery, and transplant endpoint explicit.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: The study compared bulk slow-freezing in a blood freezer bag against multiple glass tubes. DMSO was added stepwise, removed with a sucrose dilution after thawing, and freezing-thawing profiles were matched to the conventional tube method.

excerpts.label: recovery review note
excerpts.text: Rat and canine islet recovery in freezer bags was similar to glass tubes, with roughly 92 versus 90 percent recovery in rat islets and about 79 versus 82 percent recovery in canine islets. In vitro function after thawing was equivalent between the bag and tube groups, although both remained below fresh controls.

excerpts.label: transplant review note
excerpts.text: When 2000 cryopreserved canine islets from either freezer bags or glass tubes were transplanted into diabetic nude mice, the recipients became and remained normoglycemic. The paper frames the bulk-bag workflow as a practical tissue-banking method for clinical islet-transplant programs.

records.title: CRYOGENIC STORAGE OF ISOLATED, PURIFIED PORCINE PANCREATIC ISLETS
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the indexed repository abstract snippet on 2026-03-23. The source explicitly supports morphology, in vitro function, and in vivo transplant viability after cryogenic storage.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: The indexed abstract describes cryogenic storage of isolated, purified porcine pancreatic islets followed by in vitro perifusion and transplantation into temporarily immunosuppressed diabetic mice.

excerpts.label: function and morphology review note
excerpts.text: The indexed abstract reports preserved morphological integrity together with maintained in vitro insulin secretory responses after thawing, including higher total insulin secretion under stimulatory glucose plus theophylline conditions than noncryopreserved controls.

excerpts.label: transplant review note
excerpts.text: Normoglycemia was restored within 7 days after implantation of cryopreserved porcine islets into diabetic mice, and frozen-thawed graft survival was similar to noncryopreserved xenografts, supporting in vivo viability and transplantation relevance.

records.title: CRYOPRESERVATION OF CHICK ISLETS
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PMC review Modeling Chick to Assess Diabetes Pathogenesis and Treatment on 2026-03-23. The review explicitly states that the underlying chick-islet cryopreservation study preserved viability and insulin secretory activity, but the source is secondary rather than the original paper.

excerpts.label: protocol review note
excerpts.text: The accessible review states that isolated chick islets were cryopreserved using an established mouse-islet protocol in DMEM:Ham's F12 medium with fetal calf serum, riboflavin, and nicotinamide.

excerpts.label: viability and function review note
excerpts.text: The review explicitly states that chick islets could be cryopreserved without losing viability and insulin secretory activity, supporting conservative viability and function labels for the underlying study.

records.title: Cryopreservation of Freshly Isolated Porcine Islet Cells
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract explicitly supports viability and glucose-dependent function across freezing media, but not transplantation.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Freshly isolated porcine islet cells were cryopreserved in three freezing media containing either dimethyl sulfoxide or glycerol with sucrose, and post-thaw viability plus insulin production were measured after thawing.

excerpts.label: viability review note
excerpts.text: Post-thaw viability remained high in the best-performing freezing media, with about 98 percent viability in one dimethyl sulfoxide condition and about 93 percent viability in the glycerol condition, versus about 86 percent in the weaker dimethyl sulfoxide medium.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: Glucose stimulation showed only small losses of insulin secretion in the best two media and a larger decrease in glucose-dependent insulin secretion in the weaker medium, supporting post-thaw functional preservation without proving transplantation outcomes.

records.title: Cryopreservation of Human Pancreatic Islets From Non-Heart-Beating Donors Using Hydroxyethyl Starch and Dimethyl Sulfoxide as Cryoprotectants
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-22. Added conservative paraphrased notes to make the human donor context, structure/function outcomes, and transplant-adjacent decision boundary explicit.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Hydroxyethyl starch was combined with DMSO to simplify freezing and thawing while reducing DMSO toxicity. The protocol was first tested in beagle islets and then applied to 12 cryopreservation cases using human islets from non-heart-beating donors.

excerpts.label: preclinical review note
excerpts.text: In the beagle preclinical study, thawed islet structure remained well preserved, recovery was about 71 percent, and the post-thaw stimulation index was about 1.8 after 4 weeks of storage.

excerpts.label: human review note
excerpts.text: Among the human donor cases, 7 of 12 thawed samples retained normal structure while 5 showed fragmentation. Static-incubation stimulation index fell on average from about 3.37 before freezing to about 1.34 after thawing, and the authors concluded that low-function islet preparations should not be banked for transplantation even though cryopreservation was feasible.

records.title: Differential Freezing Tolerance of Rat Pancreatic Islets Depending on Their Size Variation
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible J-STAGE abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract explicitly supports function and morphology, with size-dependent freezing injury in large islets.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Freshly isolated rat pancreatic islets were grouped by size and cryopreserved with dimethyl sulfoxide or ethylene glycol at a slow cooling rate, then tested after thawing in sequential low-high-low glucose incubations.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: Insulin release from large islets was significantly suppressed after freezing in both dimethyl sulfoxide and ethylene glycol, while small- and medium-sized islets did not differ materially from unfrozen controls.

excerpts.label: morphology review note
excerpts.text: The percentage of cells containing beta granules was negatively correlated with islet size after freezing, indicating size-dependent structural injury that paralleled the functional deficit in large islets.

records.title: Nylon Mesh Device for Vitriﬁcation of Large Quantities of Rat Pancreatic Islets
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract explicitly supports post-warm survival and glucose-stimulated function, plus scale-up handling relevance, but not transplantation.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Rat islets were vitrified either with a Cryotop device or a nylon mesh device, or conventionally frozen with a Bicell vessel, and the nylon mesh approach was then scaled from 10 to 100 islets per device.

excerpts.label: viability review note
excerpts.text: Post-warm survival was about 68 percent for Cryotop vitrification and about 64 percent for nylon mesh vitrification, versus about 48 percent for conventional freezing.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion remained superior in the vitrification groups compared with the freezing group, and increasing the number of islets per nylon mesh device did not worsen cryosurvival or insulin secretion potential.

records.title: Supplementary cryoprotective effect of carboxylated ε-poly-L-lysine during vitriﬁcation of rat pancreatic islets
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-22. Added conservative paraphrased notes to make the CPLL additive effect, function, and scale-up angle explicit.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: Rat pancreatic islets were vitrified by Cryotop using ethylene glycol at 30 percent with carboxylated epsilon-poly-L-lysine at 0, 10, or 20 percent. The study also tested lower ethylene glycol concentrations with 20 percent CPLL and a larger-load nylon-mesh format.

excerpts.label: survival review note
excerpts.text: Post-warm survival was highest with 30 percent ethylene glycol plus 20 percent CPLL at about 74 percent, compared with about 65 to 66 percent in the lower-CPLL conditions. Reducing ethylene glycol to 10 or 20 percent while keeping 20 percent CPLL impaired survival.

excerpts.label: function and scale review note
excerpts.text: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion with 30 percent ethylene glycol plus 20 percent CPLL remained comparable to fresh controls and to vitrification with 30 percent ethylene glycol alone. Using nylon mesh, 50 islets per device could still be vitrified with about 68 percent survival and a stimulation index around 3.7.

records.title: USE OF POLYETHYLENEGLYCOL FOR PORCINE ISLET CRYOPRESERVATION
records.rationale: available title/abstract text is mostly procedural and does not state a concrete outcome
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewed from the accessible PubMed abstract on 2026-03-23. The abstract explicitly supports in vitro function and transplantation relevance for PEG relative to the standard dimethyl sulfoxide procedure.

excerpts.label: methods review note
excerpts.text: One-week cultured porcine islets were cryopreserved overnight in liquid nitrogen with polyethylene glycol and compared against the standard dimethyl sulfoxide procedure using in vitro glucose-response tests and mouse implantation.

excerpts.label: function review note
excerpts.text: PEG-cryopreserved islets secreted more insulin than dimethyl sulfoxide-treated islets, retained glucose-dependent insulin secretion across a wide glucose range, and were as functional in vitro as nonfrozen tissue.

excerpts.label: transplant review note
excerpts.text: When implanted in mice, PEG-cryopreserved islets reversed experimental diabetes for longer periods than noncryopreserved islets, supporting transplant relevance for PEG-based porcine islet storage.
